description: Demo flow, deployment preparation, and documentation. Create seed script for Part 4 demo data (café video brief, agreement, deliveries with inspection results), reset script, health check endpoint, deployment docs (build/start commands, env vars, Supabase Storage setup, media dependencies), architecture doc, demo script for judges. Update KIRO_PROGRESS.md with Part 4 completion summary.
steps: Create scripts/seed-demo-part4.ts: (1) Import existing seed utilities from lib/supabase-admin.ts (or create if needed). (2) Create brand user 'Demo Brand Café' if not exists. (3) Create creator user 'Demo Creator Vertical' if not exists with relevant portfolio. (4) Create brief: '15-second vertical café video for Instagram Reels', contentType='Short-form Video', aspectRatios=['9:16'], durationSeconds=15, budgetMin=1000, budgetMax=2000, status='Open'. Add issue: aspect ratio not specified in original brief text (will be caught by brief intelligence). (5) Create proposal from creator: price=1500, timelineDays=7, status='Accepted'. (6) Create agreement from proposal: version=1, deliverables from brief, both_accepted=true. (7) Note: Actual file uploads cannot be seeded via script (require multipart upload). Document manual demo steps in demo script instead.

Create scripts/reset-demo-part4.ts: (1) Delete all project_messages, scope_changes, deliveries, agreements WHERE agreement created_at > (select created_at from agreements order by created_at desc limit 1 offset 5) to preserve any earlier data. (2) Delete demo brief created in seed-demo-part4. (3) Delete demo users created in seed. (4) Add safety check: only run if NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL contains 'localhost' OR explicit --force flag passed. (5) Log what was deleted. (6) Add comment: This never affects real users, only demo data created by seed-demo-part4.

Create app/api/health/route.ts: (1) Export async GET function. (2) Check Supabase connection: try simple query SELECT 1. (3) Return 200 JSON: {status: 'healthy', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), database: 'connected', storage: 'available', version: process.env.npm_package_version || 'unknown'}. (4) If database check fails, return 503 JSON: {status: 'unhealthy', error: message}. (5) No authentication required for health check.

Create deployment/README.md: (1) Build command: npm run build (requires Node 18+). (2) Start command: npm run start (or next start). (3) Environment variables table: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL (required), NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (required), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (required), GEMINI_API_KEY (optional), NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (required, full URL with protocol). (4) Supabase Storage setup: Create 'deliveries' bucket as PRIVATE via dashboard or SQL: INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('deliveries', 'deliveries', false). Apply storage policies from database/migrations/002_delivery_workflow.sql. (5) Media inspection dependencies: sharp installed via npm (automatic). ffprobe optional - if unavailable, video inspection returns 'unsupported' status (acceptable for demo, no false passes). (6) Database migrations: Run database/migrations/002_delivery_workflow.sql in Supabase SQL Editor. (7) Health check: GET /api/health returns 200 when healthy. (8) Persistent storage: Supabase Storage handles all file persistence, no local filesystem required. (9) Port: Next.js defaults to 3000, configurable via PORT env var.

Create deployment/architecture.md: (1) System overview diagram (ASCII art): Browser → Next.js API → Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth + Storage + Realtime). (2) Data model section: users → creator_profiles/brand_profiles, briefs → proposals → agreements, agreements → deliveries + project_messages + scope_changes, reviews link agreements. (3) Agreement version flow: proposal accepted → agreement v1 created → both parties accept → production starts → creator uploads deliveries (versioned) → brand approves → project complete. (4) Delivery inspection flow: file uploaded → stored in private bucket → inspected (sharp for images, ffprobe for video if available) → results stored in JSONB → brand sees pass/fail → approves or requests revision. (5) Security model: RLS policies enforce participant-only access to agreements/deliveries/messages, storage policies restrict access by path, no public delivery URLs. (6) Limitations: Video inspection requires ffprobe (not available in all deployments), unsupported formats cannot be inspected but are clearly labeled, no tamper-proof guarantees without cryptographic signatures.

Create deployment/demo-script.md: (1) Judge access section: URL, 1-click login as brand or creator. (2) Part 4 demo flow: Login as brand → Navigate to Briefs → Create new brief '15-second vertical café video for Instagram Reels' → AI Brief Builder suggests fields → Brief Intelligence flags missing aspect ratio → Add 9:16 aspect ratio → Publish → See Top Matches with café portfolio samples → Accept proposal from matched creator → Agreement created → Both parties navigate to /projects/{agreementId} → Creator accepts agreement → Brand accepts agreement → Agreement status becomes Active → Creator uploads delivery (16:9 horizontal video provided as test asset at public/demo/cafe-horizontal.mp4) → Inspection FAILS (expected 9:16, got 16:9) → Brand sees failed inspection → Creator uploads corrected delivery (9:16 vertical video at public/demo/cafe-vertical.mp4) → Inspection PASSES → Brand approves delivery → Status becomes Completed → View Production Passport showing full journey → Brand submits review. (3) Provide actual test video assets or document where to obtain them (royalty-free stock from Pexels/Pixabay). (4) Reset instructions: Run npm run reset-demo-part4 to clear demo data.

Create PART4_IMPLEMENTATION.md: (1) Features implemented section: Versioned agreements, Private delivery uploads, Media inspection (image: sharp, video: ffprobe with graceful fallback), Feedback system, Approval workflow, Production Passport. (2) API routes added table with method/path/description. (3) Database schema changes: 4 new tables, 1 storage bucket. (4) UI components added: Project workspace with 5 tabs, DeliveryUpload, InspectionResults, ApprovalButton, ProductionPassport timeline. (5) Known limitations: ffprobe may not be available (video inspection gracefully returns 'unsupported'), no automated tests (manual verification performed), no cryptographic tamper-proofing (labeled honestly), file size limit 500MB, 1-hour signed URL expiry. (6) External setup required: Run migration 002, create deliveries bucket, install sharp (automatic via npm).

Update KIRO_PROGRESS.md: (1) Add Part 4 Completion Summary section. (2) Completed tasks: Database schema extended, Agreement/delivery API routes, Media inspection library, Project workspace UI, Feedback and approval system, Production Passport, Health check endpoint, Deployment docs, Demo flow. (3) Tests actually run table: Build check (npm run build), Manual API tests with Postman/curl listing specific endpoints tested, Database verification queries run, UI functionality tests in browser (specific pages/features). (4) Tests NOT run: End-to-end automated tests (none written), Video inspection with actual ffprobe (may not be available in all environments - graceful fallback verified instead). (5) Configuration requirements: Supabase Storage 'deliveries' bucket (private), Migration 002 applied, sharp installed. (6) Scoring logic: Media inspection tolerances (aspect ratio ±1%, duration ±0.5s, resolution exact), pass/fail/unsupported/error statuses. (7) Limitations: Video inspection requires ffprobe (graceful fallback if unavailable), no real-time preview during upload, no bulk delivery uploads, no PDF export of Production Passport (visual only). (8) Remaining work: None for Part 4 scope. Future enhancements could include automated tests, PDF generation, bulk uploads. (9) Deployment ready: Yes, with documented setup steps.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/seed-demo-part4.ts creates demo brand, creator, brief, proposal, and agreement with valid data structure
scripts/reset-demo-part4.ts safely deletes only demo data, includes localhost check, logs deleted records
app/api/health/route.ts returns 200 with database connected status when healthy, 503 when database unreachable, no auth required
deployment/README.md contains complete build/start commands, all env vars with descriptions, Supabase Storage setup steps, media dependencies notes, migration instructions, health check usage
deployment/architecture.md explains system overview, data model with relationships, agreement/delivery workflow, inspection flow, security model, documented limitations
deployment/demo-script.md provides step-by-step judge demo flow matching the Part 4 requirements (café video, horizontal fails, vertical passes), includes reset instructions
PART4_IMPLEMENTATION.md summarizes all features implemented, API routes, schema changes, UI components, known limitations, external setup
KIRO_PROGRESS.md updated with Part 4 summary distinguishing tests actually run from tests not run, documents configuration, scoring logic, limitations honestly
verification: Run npm run db:seed-demo-part4 (after implementing script). Verify no errors. Query database: SELECT * FROM agreements WHERE version=1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1. Expect demo agreement exists.
Test health check: curl http://localhost:3000/api/health. Expect 200 response with {status: 'healthy', database: 'connected'}. Stop Supabase (or break connection), retry, expect 503 or error status.
Read deployment/README.md: Verify all required env vars documented, build/start commands correct, storage setup steps clear. Follow setup steps in fresh environment to validate completeness.

Read deployment/architecture.md: Verify data model section accurately reflects actual schema from database/migrations/002_delivery_workflow.sql. Check limitations section honestly states no tamper-proofing.

Read deployment/demo-script.md: Verify demo flow matches Part 4 requirements (15-second vertical café video, brief issue identified, horizontal delivery fails, vertical passes, approval, passport shows journey). Check test asset paths or procurement instructions provided.
Read PART4_IMPLEMENTATION.md: Cross-reference API routes table with actual files created in app/api/. Verify limitations section includes 'ffprobe may not be available'.

Read KIRO_PROGRESS.md Part 4 section: Verify 'Tests actually run' includes specific commands executed (npm run build, specific curl/Postman requests). Verify 'Tests NOT run' section exists and includes 'End-to-end automated tests'. Verify limitations section includes video inspection fallback.
Final build check: npm run build. Expect 0 TypeScript errors (prerender warnings acceptable).
